name: CO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+29 partisan lean in a heavily Democratic Denver-based seat
Melat Kiros has raised over $1 million plus outside support, dwarfing the Republican's ~$2,000
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee at 98%
Open seat after DeGette lost renomination, but the seat stays with the incumbent party
model.rationale: CO-01's D+29 lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely even without an incumbent on the ballot. Kiros's massive fundraising edge over Peterson and a 98% market price confirm the fundamentals, so the forecast stays at the district's baseline margin.
model.watch: A surprise third-party surge or unusually low Democratic turnout in an open-seat year could trim the margin, though not the likely winner.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Diana DeGette (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Denver-based CO-01 is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a D+29 partisan lean. Longtime incumbent Diana DeGette lost renomination, so this is an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Melat Kiros starts with every structural advantage. She has raised over $1.1 million and drawn substantial outside spending, while Republican Christy Peterson has raised only about $2,000.

Prediction markets give the Democratic nominee roughly a 98% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects a comfortable Democratic victory on the order of thirty points, consistent with the district's fundamentals.
